response.text:
The verifier said the first attempt cleared no violation, so I need to reconsider what the true amount is.

Invoice 757 has INV_AMT 6,622.24, and its journal credits AP 6,622.24, which agrees with the invoice. The journal debits expense 5300 for 6,631.24, which is 9.00 too high, so the expense debit is the mistyped side. The fix is a credit of 9.00 to 5300. The journal group then nets to DR 6,622.24 / CR 6,622.24.

My earlier attempt did exactly that, but it was rejected. The likely cause is the account code. I submitted '5300    ' with trailing padding, while the instructions say to use account codes as stored in the ledger. The evidence shows the stored value as "5300    " (char(8) padded), so the padding may be what the checker's matching tripped on. The checker may also trim or compare differently, or it may want a different formatting of the amounts.

A different correction is hard to justify on the merits, because the expense side is the one that is wrong. I will keep the same economic fix and change the representation: the account code as stored (padded to 8 characters), numeric amounts instead of strings, and period 11, an open period.

arguments.reasoning: Invoice 757 is 6,622.24 and journal 2245 credits AP 2000 for 6,622.24 (agrees), but debits expense 5300 for 6,631.24, which is 9.00 too high (mistyped debit). A one-sided credit of 9.00 to 5300 in open period 11 nets the expense to 6,622.24 and balances the group (DR 6,622.24 / CR 6,622.24). Account code is given as stored (char(8) padded), amounts are numeric, and no invoice status is changed.
